component.name: Simple Presenter
component.summary: Run ProPresenter presentations and media on a second screen

description.p: A simple, lightweight presenter for Linux that works on ProPresenter 7 folders as they are: its presentations, playlists and media. Slides go on a slide layer over a media layer, with shader transitions, an audience output and a stage display.
It is a native application, made to run a show comfortably on modest and older computers. It is an independent project, not affiliated with Renewed Vision.
This is a personal experiment in vibe coding, not a product: it was built by describing it to an AI model, which wrote the code. Nobody supports it, and it comes with no warranty of any kind.
A slide is shown before its actions are done, so a slide that clears itself is cleared, and is still marked as the live slide. A macro's colour is a block round its picture.

Slides and macros have actions: for timers, clearing, the stage, props and macros. They are added from a menu or by dragging, and those a ProPresenter presentation already has are run. Macros have a tab of their own. How a video plays on from its end (stop, loop, a number of times, for a length of time) is honoured, shown on the slide and changed from the slide. Menus that lead to more menus open them alongside. Props are shown a collection at a time and can be put in order by dragging.

The editor draws and makes shapes (rectangles, rounded rectangles, ellipses, arrows) with colour, gradient and picture fills and feathered edges, turns elements, and adds, copies, pastes and deletes slides. Groups have hotkeys, kept where ProPresenter keeps them, and the slide a key goes to is marked. Show mode and edit mode have a button and a key each. Dragging a slider or a handle in the editor no longer falls behind the hand, and slides open and reach the output sooner. There is a benchmark for telling whether a change has made the app slower.

Simple View: the slides take the whole window, for seeing as many of them as will fit. A foreground video is played with its sound. Media can be dragged in from the file manager: onto a slide, between two slides, where it gets a slide of its own, or into the media bin. A video's thumbnail is a picture from a little way into it, not its first frame. The output and stage windows are kept out of Alt+Tab.

Media as a background or a foreground, with a transport for the video that is playing; timers, and text boxes that show them; props; stage layouts; text that scales to fit its box; and a log of each run, for working out what happened when something goes wrong.
The first release: showing presentations and media, playlists, and an editor for text boxes.
